text: Everyone says the new course is faster but the results don't show it. Median finish was 3:58 last year on the old route and 3:56 this year. Two minutes across 4,000 runners is noise, not a faster course.
label: analysis

text: Looked at my last three build-ups. The one where I capped long runs at 2 hours had my best race by 4 minutes, despite the lowest weekly mileage of the three. Time on feet past 2 hours was costing me the next four days.
label: analysis

text: The 10% rule doesn't survive contact with actual training logs. I went from 30 to 50 miles a week over six weeks last autumn with no issues, and got injured the year before going up 8% a week. Consistency mattered more than the increment.
label: analysis

text: Checked the splits from the top 20 finishers. Eighteen of them ran the second half slower, average positive split of 3:40. On a course billed as net downhill. Something about the back section is harder than the elevation profile suggests.
label: analysis

text: Carbon plates gave me about 2% on paper and roughly nothing in races. Three time trials in each shoe on the same loop, same month: 19:42/19:38/19:51 in the plates, 19:47/19:55/19:44 in the trainers. The overlap is bigger than the gap.
label: analysis

text: My heart rate drift over 90 minutes dropped from 11% to 4% across a year of easy running with no change in pace. That's the aerobic base people talk about, and it took eleven months to show up in the numbers.
label: analysis

text: Six of the last eight course records here were set in years when race-day temperature was under 10C. The two exceptions were both years with a strong tailwind on the back half. Weather explains more of the record book than the field does.
label: analysis

text: Ran the same 5k route weekly for a year, 47 runs. The variance by day of week was larger than my improvement over the middle six months. Tuesday runs averaged 22 seconds faster than Saturday ones, and I think it's just that Saturdays followed long runs.
label: analysis

text: The entry fee went from 45 to 72 over four years. Field size went from 3,200 to 3,400. Whatever the extra 27 is paying for, it isn't capacity.
label: analysis

text: Went back through my logs for every race where I hit my goal. All four had a three-week taper. The two where I tapered for ten days I missed by over two minutes. Small sample, but it's the only variable that lines up.
label: analysis

text: The women's field here has grown 60% in five years while the men's is flat. That's the actual story of this race and nobody writes about it.
label: analysis

text: Tried the low-carb approach for eight weeks. Easy pace at the same heart rate dropped by 15 seconds a mile and never came back until I reintroduced carbohydrate. Whatever it does for fat oxidation, it cost me aerobic pace.
label: analysis

text: Compared finishing times for people who did the club's structured plan against those who self-coached. Structured group averaged 6 minutes faster, but they also averaged 8 more miles a week. The plan may just be a mileage delivery mechanism.
label: analysis

text: Three of my last five injuries came within two weeks of a shoe change. I'm not saying the shoes caused it, but I've stopped changing models in a build-up.
label: analysis

text: Split the field by finish time and looked at DNF rates. Under 3:30, about 1%. Over 5 hours, about 9%. The cutoff is at 6 hours and the aid stations start closing at 5:15, which might explain more of that than fitness does.
label: analysis

text: Elevation gain on the official profile is 340m. My watch says 410m and so do the four other people I've compared with. The profile is either smoothed or wrong, and it matters for pacing the last 10k.
label: analysis

text: Went through five years of my own training. Every year my best race followed a block with at least eight weeks of uninterrupted running. Every year I got injured, it was in a week where I'd added both mileage and intensity.
label: analysis

text: The pace group at 3:30 finished in 3:34 last year and 3:31 the year before. If you're using them as a safety net, know that the net has a hole in it roughly every other year.
label: analysis

text: Bought a treadmill in January and my outdoor pace got worse by about 10 seconds a mile through February. Same heart rate, same effort. I think the treadmill was flattering me on effort and I'd stopped running hills entirely.
label: analysis

text: Twelve weeks of doubles versus twelve weeks of single runs at the same weekly volume. Doubles block: more consistent, no missed days, race 90 seconds faster. Singles block: two missed weeks from fatigue. For me the split makes the volume survivable.
label: analysis
